chunks: Ibrāhīm ibn Maymūn said to him:
We go out to al-Ahwāz in ships, and we combine the salat (prayer) in them. So he said: “Yes, there is no harm in that.”
So he said to him: Then do we perform sajdah (prostration) upon what is in them and upon pitch? He said: “There is no harm.”

key_terms.السُّفُنِ: ships or vessels used for travel
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being discussed
key_terms.الْأَهْوَازِ: al-Ahwāz, the destination mentioned in the journey
key_terms.الْقِيرِ: pitch or tar, a material mentioned as a surface for prostration
key_terms.بَأْسٌ: harm or objection, indicating permissibility when negated
key_terms.فَنَسْجُدُ: then we prostrate, referring to sajdah
key_terms.فَنُجَمِّعُ: we combine, referring to combining prayers

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to combine prayers and prostrate on a ship or on pitch during travel?
ai.summary: This hadith states that combining salat (prayer) while traveling by ship to al-Ahwāz is permitted. It also indicates that performing sajdah (prostration) on the surface available in the ship, including pitch, is allowed, showing ease in rulings during travel circumstances.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1322 - Ibrahim ibn Maymun said to him (Abu Abdullah (as)):

"We travel to Ahwaz in ships, and we combine the prayers on board."
He (as) replied: "Yes, there is no harm in that."

He further asked: "And we prostrate on what is in the ship and on the pitch (tar)?"
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm."
